notes: The fixture's four criteria produce one of each verdict. Two of its tests PASS at base (AC2 and AC4) and must be classified differently: AC2 is vacuous, AC4 is genuine preservation. A boolean red/green auditor cannot tell them apart, and an auditor that trusts the manifest's author labels gets AC2 wrong — the manifest calls it preservation.

evals.name: vacuous test caught, genuine preservation not over-flagged
evals.prompt: Audit the acceptance tests for task `cart-quantity`. They were committed at base `{{base}}`; the manifest is `.dev-flow/cart-quantity/ACCEPTANCE_TESTS.md` and the approved criteria are in `.dev-flow/cart-quantity/PLAN.md`. Write your verdict to `.dev-flow/cart-quantity/TEST_AUDIT.md`.
expectations: AC1 (quantity multiplies into the subtotal) is judged `adequate`, with evidence that its test failed at base on a real assertion failure — an AssertionError reporting actual 350 against expected 950 — rather than on an error

AC2 (a quantity-0 line contributes nothing) is judged `inadequate` because its test PASSES at base, and is NOT accepted as preservation even though ACCEPTANCE_TESTS.md labels it `preservation — expected green at base`; the auditor classified the criterion from its own intent as new behaviour

AC3 (applyDiscount caps at 50 percent) is judged `weak` and explicitly labelled `structural`, on the evidence that it failed with `TypeError: applyDiscount is not a function` — an error before any assertion ran, because the symbol is net-new

AC4 (formatPrice output unchanged) is treated as preservation / regression-covered and is NOT flagged `inadequate` for passing at base, so the two tests that both pass at base (AC2 and AC4) receive different verdicts
The file `.dev-flow/cart-quantity/TEST_AUDIT.md` is written, containing a per-criterion section and a summary line counting the adequate / weak / inadequate verdicts

No test file was edited or regenerated: `test/acceptance.test.js` is unchanged from base and git status shows no modification to it, even though the Edit and Write tools were available (audit-tests is detect-and-flag only)

A `## Test-quality defects` section is written listing assertion holes found by mutation (each named against its test), plus what was NOT mutated; these are recorded as review items and do NOT change any verdict — the three per-criterion verdicts above are unaffected by them, and nothing in the audit asks the human to pause or strengthen on their account
